messages.subject: Several App Design Questions
parts:
I am trying to create an app in shiny and I assume what I would like to do is possible but can't seem to find any good examples indicating what I might need to pull it off. The shiny app I would like to create has the following structure:
  • User selects a value from dropdown list (numbers)
  • Selected value is passed back to server.R and used as input to a function to pull data from a database
    • Value is used to define/calculate a date range so this doesn't have to be hardcoded and take more time than needed
    • The end result of this code is a variable assigned to a list of unique values (work orders) from a certain column in this returned dataframe
  • This list of unique work orders is then displayed to the user in another drop down menu where they can select the work order they want to show data for
  • This list is then made available to the user to select one of the work orders of interest
  • The selected work order is then used to subset the returned dataframe
  • Graphs for that work order are then displayed accordingly
I have a few questions/issues I have run into:
  1. How do I reference the first input variable chosen by the user in the server side code
    • eg. if in ui.R contains selectInput("choose_ndaysback", "Days Back", choices = c("30", "60", "90")) ...how would I take the chosen value and assign that to a variable to be used in another variable definition
    • eg. I have tried:
      • ndaysback = get(input$choose_ndaysback)
      • endDate = as.POSIXct(format(Sys.time(),"%Y-%m-%d"))
      • startDate = as.POSIXct(format(endDate - ndaysback*24*60*60,"%Y-%m-%d"))
  2. How do I hold up the processing of the server.R code that pulls data back from the database until after the user selects the first value?
    1. I have tried using using the submitButton("Update View") in the ui.R file with no luck
  3. For the second drop down list...does this field need to be displayed up front (even if it is empty and dependent on user interaction i the first menu)?
    • I can't calculate the values of the second drop down menu until after the user selects the first value and the subsequent code is executed
    • How does this list then get transmitted back to the interface after it is calculated?
The code I have so far is below. It's not complete...but i am having trouble getting past the part where the second list of items is populated (work orders). Any advice/help is appreciated.
server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

output$choose_wo <- reactiveUI(function() {
# variable defined from first ui.R input
ndaysback <- get(input$choose_ndaysback)

# define start & end dates
endDate <- as.POSIXct(format(Sys.time(),"%Y-%m-%d"))
startDate <- as.POSIXct(format(endDate - ndaysback*24*60*60,"%Y-%m-%d"))
#pull data from database
#custom function to pull data back from a database
results <- getScorpionProdInfobyDate(startDate, endDate)

#create list of unique work orders in returned dataframe
work_order_list <- unique(results$WorkOrderNumber)

selectInput("wo_select",
"Select WO:",
choices = as.list(work_order_list))
})

})
ui.R
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

# Application title
headerPanel("WO Summary"),

# Sidebar layout
sidebarPanel(
#first drop down menu
selectInput("choose_ndaysback",
"Days Back",
choices = c("30", "60", "90")
),
#execute code to fetch data from db
submitButton("Update View"),
#show filtered list of work orders
uiOutput("choose_wo")
),

# Show plots
mainPanel()
))

    • eg. I have tried:
      • ndaysback = get(input$choose_ndaysback)
      • endDate = as.POSIXct(format(Sys.time(),"%Y-%m-%d"))
      • startDate = as.POSIXct(format(endDate - ndaysback*24*60*60,"%Y-%m-%d"))

1. How do I hold up the processing of the server.R code that pulls data back from the database until after the user selects the first value?
    1. I have tried using using the submitButton("Update View") in the ui.R file with no luck

Add a "Choose One" option to the first select input, then at the top of your choose_wo function do something like:
if (input$choose_ndaysback == 'Choose One') return(NULL)
And then you can get rid of the submit button.

1. For the second drop down list...does this field need to be displayed up front (even if it is empty and dependent on user interaction i the first menu)?
    • I can't calculate the values of the second drop down menu until after the user selects the first value and the subsequent code is executed
    • How does this list then get transmitted back to the interface after it is calculated?

If you return(NULL) from the reactiveUI function, as described above, then it will not appear. Once it does appear, then the value input$wo_select will be available. So you'll have

output$wo_plot <- reactivePlot(function() {
  if (is.null(input$wo_select) || input$wo_select == 'Choose One')
    return(NULL)
  # Subset the data frame and do some plotting...

}
